findings.observation: The actual pitch-energy curves show the upper grace pitch rising before the principal pitch at all three corresponding score passages. Candidate attack-peak gaps are about 20–30 ms. This supports a two-attack interpretation, not calibrated physical onset precision.

Two grace pitches precede a chord containing one of those pitches. Using the chord's exclusive C5 as a witness reveals a clearer later attack than comparing the grace to the same-pitch chord note. Candidate ordering is plausible on the displayed curves.

A strong C5 energy rise occurs before the narrow search window; the algorithm instead chooses a small later change near the coarse onset. The existing score plus this plot does not disambiguate preceding-note decay from the grace attack. Do not accept the narrow-window result.
The grace-pitch envelope starts rising before the selected local derivative peak. The selected peak may describe a second envelope change, so peak time cannot be treated as physical note onset.

Both displayed pitch envelopes have their main attack before the selected candidates. The coarse alignment has drifted far enough that the narrow-window refinement selects later fluctuations. Correct the coarse anchor first.

The machine returns identical grace and main times. In measures 65 and 69 the displayed principal-pitch rise is visibly later; the search window/main-witness choice has not resolved it. Equal timestamps are an explicit gap, not simultaneous acceptance.
The selected grace-pitch time lies on a low fluctuating envelope with another large later attack. The local view does not justify a particular grace-to-main assignment.
